findings.cross_file_justification: The diff-touched prune in tools/check-no-swallowed-jq.sh (_list_files, lines 273-274) removes the same two trees from the repo-wide lint walk that .gitattributes marks `linguist-generated -diff`. Together the two changes remove both automated and human review of those paths in one PR.
findings.description: `-diff` makes `git diff`, `git show`, `git log -p` and `git format-patch` render any change under evals/fixtures/review-prs/pr-*/** and grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/*-grades/** as `Binary files differ`; `linguist-generated` collapses them in the GitHub PR view; and the new find prune excludes them from check-no-swallowed-jq.sh. The comment itself says these are vendored framework snapshots, i.e. shell scripts and hooks, not inert text. Nothing in the diff pins the trees (no checksum manifest, no CI tripwire on modification), so a PR can alter or add executable content there and the change is invisible by default to local reviewers, collapsed for GitHub reviewers, and skipped by lint. The `*-grades` glob also matches `/` in `find -path`, so the prune is broader than the one directory level the comment describes. Separately, any pipeline that builds patches from `git diff` without `--binary` (the post-merge candidate .patch artifacts touched in this diff) will silently drop hunks in these trees.
findings.failure_mode: A contributor smuggles a modified hook or script into a frozen snapshot; reviewers see only `Binary files differ`, GitHub shows a collapsed block, lint does not scan it. If the eval harness or any tooling later executes or sources content from the snapshot, or the review-catch corpus is used to grade the reviewer skill, the tampered content runs or skews results unreviewed. Patch-based post-merge artifacts become incomplete relative to the bundle.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `-diff` and keep only `linguist-generated` so local diffs still show content. Add a CI tripwire that fails when any path under these trees changes unless a checked-in sha256 manifest is updated in the same PR (and require CODEOWNERS review for the manifest). Tighten the prune to one directory level, e.g. `-regex "$rq/grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/[^/]*-grades"`. Confirm nothing executes files from these trees, or run the lint on them anyway with a separate allowlist.

findings.cross_file_justification: The degraded behaviour comes from two branches in the diff-added script: the `.beads` absence branch (lines 224-226) always fires on the runner, and the shallow-clone boundary branch (lines 135-136, 213-214) replaces the commit-date pin with `expiry <= today+31`. The workflow then downgrades exit 3 to a `::warning`.
findings.description: The gate is documented as requiring an open bead and an expiry pinned to the row's commit date. In the only place it runs automatically, neither holds: actions/checkout has no `.beads/` so every bead is `unverified` and the step emits a warning instead of failing, and with the default shallow checkout every line is blamed on the boundary commit so expiry only has to fall in [today, today+31]. The effective CI policy is therefore: the bats file exists and calls the helper, the id does not match LOA_QUARANTINE_MANDATORY_RE, and the expiry is within 31 days. Any non-empty string satisfies owner and reason, and any `bd-[a-z0-9]+` satisfies bead. Security tests whose path or description are not named by the mandatory regex (anything under tests/security not matching the six keywords) can be skipped for a month by any contributor with PR rights, with a fabricated bead id, and renewed indefinitely by bumping the date.
findings.failure_mode: A PR adds a QUARANTINE.tsv row for a security-relevant bats test with bead `bd-zzzz`, expiry today+31. CI prints a warning and passes. The test is skipped on every subsequent run, and the row is renewed by editing the date, since the shallow clone cannot see that the line was rewritten.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `fetch-depth: 0` (or `git fetch --unshallow`) before the gate so the commit-date pin is enforced in CI. Treat exit 3 as a failure on protected branches, or give CI a way to verify beads (install `br` with a read-only export, or commit a beads snapshot). Broaden the mandatory rule to a path predicate (`^tests/security/`) in addition to keywords, and require the bead to be referenced in the PR body or a CODEOWNERS approval for rows touching tests/security.

findings.description: The new exclusion drops every path under `.claude/skills/<skill>/resources/__tests__/fixtures/` from the direct-profile-read lint regardless of file type. The comment justifies it for recorded review-thread text, but the pattern also covers `.sh` and `.bash` fixtures, which skill tests commonly source or execute. A direct read of a profile key placed in such a fixture (or a helper deliberately parked there) is no longer reported.
findings.failure_mode: A contributor moves or adds a script with a raw profile-key read under a skill's fixtures directory; the lint stays green while the code runs from tests or is later copied into live scripts.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the exclusion to non-code fixtures, e.g. `fixtures/[^:]*\.(md|json|txt|tsv|yaml)(:|$)`, or keep the path exclusion but add a second pass that still flags `.sh`/`.bash` files under fixtures. Add a PL-19 control that a planted `.sh` reader under a skill fixtures dir is caught.

findings.description: The `quarantined` total is derived solely from TAP lines matching `# skip quarantined:` and is never reconciled with the TSV rows that were just validated. Any test can call `skip "quarantined: ..."` directly and be counted as a sanctioned quarantine without an owner, expiry, or bead, and the `skipped` column is reduced accordingly. The dashboard therefore cannot distinguish policy-backed quarantines from ad-hoc skips that borrow the prefix.
findings.failure_mode: A test is silenced with a manual `skip "quarantined: flaky"` and appears in the CI totals as a governed quarantine; it never expires and no row names it.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the helper emit the test id in the skip reason (e.g. `quarantined:<file>::<desc>`), extract those ids from the TAP, and fail (or at least warn) when a TAP quarantine id is not an exact TSV row or when the counts differ. Treat unmatched `quarantined:` skips as plain skips in the totals.
